what: Potential viral hook identified: instant codebase-to-rules generation. "One command, your agent knows your whole project." User runs npx aide-memory init --scan → gets CLAUDE.md + .cursorrules generated in 30 seconds from codebase analysis. Immediate dopamine hit in minute 1, not "over time your agent gets better." The pattern for viral dev tools: solves a pain you feel RIGHT NOW with immediate relief (like Cursor, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, Docker). Memory/team sharing/governance is the retention engine, but the viral moment is the instant scan. This reframes the product: the HOOK is instant codebase understanding, the PRODUCT is persistent memory + team context.
why: User asked "what is that same vibe as OpenClaw" — looking for the viral energy. The instant scan → generated config files could be the viral hook that makes people share aide-memory, while the memory engine is what keeps them using it. This could change the go-to-market strategy significantly.
